newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Power failure hits Hongkong Bank computers.
newsitem.headline: Power failure hits Hongkong Bank computers.

text.p: Hong Kong shoppers seeking cash were frustrated on Thursday when a power failure at Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd's computer centre stopped operation of all of the bank's automated teller machines (ATMs).
"Just after 11 o'clock (0300 GMT) we had a failure with certain power equipment which powers up our computer centres," said Malcolm Gray, Hongkong Bank's head of technology.
"We have some equipment which is called uninterruptible power supply, and that is what has been interrupted."
A Hongkong Bank spokesman said the power failure lasted for about one hour.
The bank's more than 800 ATMs, including those of subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd, took somewhat longer to come back online as the system was revived in stages.
Computer connections with branches were also lost, although customers were able to conduct simple transactions that could be handled by each branch's inhouse computers, he said.
Complex or unusually large transactions requiring access to the central computers would have been delayed, he added.
No customer should have suffered losses, he said, adding that all transactions that took place during the power outage had been recorded.
Trading activities at the bank's securities arms were not involved, but the spokesman said he was not certain whether interbank transactions were affected.
"We're trying to find out why there was a power outage, and it's very unusual because the failure brought down not just our main power but also the backup power," he said.
Hongkong Bank and Hang Seng Bank are members of the HSBC Holdings Plc group.
